summary: This note is a short encyclopedic entry on Martin the Humane (1356–1410), also called Martin the Elder and Martin the Ecclesiastic. It describes his long list of titles, including King of Aragon, Valencia, Sardinia and Corsica, Count of Barcelona, and King of Sicily as Martin II. It also notes that his failure to secure the succession of his illegitimate grandson Frederic, Count of Luna, ended the rule of the House of Barcelona.
one_line: Martin the Humane (1356–1410), King of Aragon and several other realms, whose failed succession plan ended the House of Barcelona's rule.
key_facts: Martin the Humane was born on 29 July 1356 and died on 31 May 1410.
Martin the Humane was also called the Elder and the Ecclesiastic.
Martin the Humane was King of Aragon, Valencia, Sardinia and Corsica.
Martin the Humane was Count of Barcelona from 1396.
Martin the Humane was King of Sicily from 1409, reigning as Martin II.
Martin the Humane failed to secure the accession of his illegitimate grandson, Frederic, Count of Luna.
The failure of Martin the Humane's succession plan brought the rule of the House of Barcelona to an end.
